collection.description: A child asks why adults can make rules that children are expected to follow.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (child) asks why adults can make rules that children are expected to follow.

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: (child) accepts the rule about sharp tools but questions an arbitrary bedtime.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: The discussion leads adults to admit that some rules are habits, not necessities.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: The children draft a surprisingly fair sharing agreement.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: Their first proposal gives children unlimited treats, and negotiation begins.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: (young), a young villager, asks whether leaders must obey the same rules.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: The group agrees that authority should come with accountability.

d2.name: Outcome D2
d2.text: (parent) hears their own harsh tone and returns later to apologize.
